overall_summary: After deduplicating 47 unique Shorts across the observation period, performance is starkly divided. First-person hypothetical space survival hooks ('What If You Fell Into...') and extreme exoplanet phenomena dominate the channel's top tier (averaging 800-1,050+ views with high like-to-view ratios exceeding 3.5%), whereas cognitive psychology, brain trivia, and generic space silence concepts consistently stall under 100 views. Videos between 19 and 21 seconds with high-stakes physical peril generate the strongest viewer retention and engagement.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,029 views, 38 likes) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (972 views, 18 likes) drastically outperform standard facts.
winning_patterns.action: Anchor future uploads on visceral, first-person scenario hooks placing the viewer inside extreme alien environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (981 views, 21 likes) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,030 views, 36 likes) show counter-intuitive planetary physics drive high click-through and shares.
winning_patterns.action: Use jarring cognitive contradictions as visual and narrative lead-ins.

weak_patterns.evidence: Multiple iterations of 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) and 'Songs Stuck In Your Head' (17-71 views) repeatedly flopped with zero engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Cease low-stakes neurological trivia and re-uploading identical hooks.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'This Star Is Older Than the Universe!' hit only 11 views, and repeated 'Why Space Is Completely Silent' uploads peaked at just 220 views.
weak_patterns.action: Eliminate static informational lectures lacking tangible sensory consequences or visual danger.
